name: Fire-Detection
description: This dataset evaluates fire detection in images. Given an image and a text prompt, the model must output bounding boxes around fire regions. It measures visual object detection capabilities for safety-critical scenarios.
card_text: Fire-Detection is a multimodal dataset of 200 image samples annotated with fire bounding boxes. Each item contains an input image path, a short user- or model-specific prompt, and an output annotation list. The output list holds one or more fire instances, where each instance is a dictionary mapping the class label 'fire' to coordinates [x, y, width, height]. Images cover real-world scenes and vary in complexity, with some samples containing single fire regions and others multiple. The text prompt serves as a detection instruction, though many entries use a generic placeholder. The dataset is designed for assessing fire localization and detection, assuming that fire is the only target class and that the model can handle varying numbers of instances.

context.semantics: A short user- or model-specific prompt that instructs the system to detect fire in the accompanying image. It serves as the textual task specification for the visual detection task.

image.semantics: The input image path referencing a real-world scene that may contain one or more fire regions. It is the visual context the model must analyze to produce bounding box annotations.

bbox.semantics: A list of fire instance annotations. Each element is a dictionary with the class label 'fire' as key and a bounding box [x, y, width, height] as value. These boxes localize fire regions in the input image.

meta.meta_structure_description: Each sample consists of three semantic components: a text prompt (input.prompt) that gives the detection instruction, an image reference (input.image_file) that provides the visual scene, and a list of fire bounding boxes (output.bbox) that gives the target spatial annotations. The prompt is a short instruction, the image is the visual context, and each bounding box entry is an object with the class name 'fire' as key and a four-number coordinate array as value. The components relate as an instruction-image-to-annotation triple for object detection.
